problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-1,\sqrt{3}⟩, \\ N(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-\sqrt{3},-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =T(\frac{\pi }{6})\times N(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-1,\sqrt{3}⟩\times \frac{1}{2}⟨0,-\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & -\sqrt{3} & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & -\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨(1+3),-(0-0),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨4,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
